summary.headline: Very safe and steadily compounding, but its idle capital keeps returns near 13%, so at Rs 215 it is about fairly priced
summary.text: Central Finance (CFIN.N0000) is one of Sri Lanka's oldest vehicle-leasing and loan companies, and also owns 21.4% of Nations Trust Bank (19.72% of the votes) and half of Central Industries (PVC pipes). It is very safe: core capital 31.9% against a 10% minimum, equity about half of group assets, gross Stage 3 loans 1.79%, and group profit every year for at least ten years. Group EPS was Rs 45.09 in 2025/26 and Rs 28.73 in the six months to September 2026 (up 17%), but that rise came from the bank: the finance company's own profit fell 14% (25% in the September quarter) as interest costs rose 76% on new borrowing and impairment reversals dried up. At Rs 215.25 (CSE, 27 November 2026) the share is 0.54x group NAV of Rs 395.47 and 4.4x trailing EPS, which looks cheap, but with a group ROE of about 13% against the 17.2% a shareholder should demand (beta 0.87), a discount to book is deserved. Four equity methods put fair value at Rs 209.91 (was Rs 219.30), so the price is about 2.5% above it: fair. I'd buy at up to Rs 178.43 and treat Rs 157.43 or lower as a strong buy. It passes three of the four business tests (fails only on returns), so it stays on the watch list.

quality.reason: Exceptionally well capitalised, profitable every year and paying every year; the weakness is a 12–14% return on equity.

tests.label: Return on equity of 15% or more
tests.note: Group ROE on average owners' equity 13.2% (2021/22), 12.5%, 12.3%, 13.7%, 12.6% (2025/26), 13.0% for the twelve months to September 2026 (calculated). Low because equity is about half of assets and a quarter of it is the bank stake.

tests.label: Capital comfortably above the minimum (finance company)
tests.note: Company, September 2026: Tier 1 31.86% (minimum 10%), total capital 30.67% (minimum 14%); down from 38.4% a year earlier as loans grew. Borrowings Rs 29.9bn, deposits Rs 51.2bn, owners' equity Rs 89.9bn.

tests.label: Steady profit: no loss in five years, no one-offs
tests.note: Group profit rose every year from 2020/21 to 2025/26. Impairment reversals helped (Rs 1.90bn in 2024/25, Rs 0.97bn in 2025/26, Rs 0.25bn in H1 2026/27) but are small next to Rs 14.2bn of profit before tax.

tests.label: Profit turns into cash and dividends
tests.note: Cash dividends every year, Rs 6.50 for 2024/25 and 2025/26, covered 4.09 times by company profit; payout is low (14% of group EPS), so book value compounds. Operating cash flow swings with loan growth (−Rs 17.7bn in 2025/26), as usual for a lender.

valuation.note: Fair value weights the bear/base/bull averages of four methods 30/50/20 (about 0.53x group NAV). No cash-flow DCF: a finance group is valued on its equity. All four methods are computed by scripts/valuation.py.

highlights.title: Six months to September 2026 (unaudited)
highlights.text: Group profit to shareholders up 17% to Rs 6.53bn (EPS Rs 28.73 against Rs 24.50), carried by a 44% rise in the share of Nations Trust Bank profit to Rs 3.33bn (Rs 2.35bn in the September quarter alone, against Rs 0.97bn in June; the interim doesn't say why). The finance company itself earned Rs 2.86bn, down 14%: interest expenses up 76%, impairment reversals down to Rs 0.26bn from Rs 0.90bn, costs up 22%.

highlights.title: Loans growing on borrowed money
highlights.text: Leases, hire purchase and loans rose 58% in 2025/26 and another 13% to Rs 118.9bn by September 2026. Borrowings went from almost nothing in March 2025 to Rs 29.9bn, alongside deposits of Rs 51.2bn. Core capital fell from 47.1% (March 2025) to 31.9%, still three times the minimum.

highlights.title: 2025/26 (audited)
highlights.text: Group profit to shareholders Rs 10.25bn (Rs 9.92bn), EPS Rs 45.09, NAV Rs 375.23. Company profit Rs 6.04bn, ROE 10.52%. Gross NPL 1.65% (2.76%). Dividend Rs 6.50, unchanged.

highlights.title: Nations Trust Bank stake must be cut
highlights.text: The group holds 19.72% of Nations Trust Bank's votes and must bring that down to 15% under the Banking Act; its votes are capped at 10% until then. At today's prices the stake is worth about Rs 99 a CF share against a book value of about Rs 103.

models.name: Justified price to book
models.comment: NAV Rs 395.47 × (long-run ROE − growth) ÷ (cost of equity − growth): ROE 11% / 12.5% / 14%, growth 5% / 6% / 7%, cost of equity 18.7% / 17.2% / 15.7% (0.44x / 0.58x / 0.80x book).

models.name: P/E on 2026/27 earnings
models.comment: 2026/27 EPS of Rs 46 / 51 / 56 at 3.5x / 4.5x / 5.5x, below the justified 4.0x / 4.6x / 5.7x. Base EPS is above the Rs 49.32 twelve-month figure but 22% below the September quarter × 4 (Rs 65.68) on purpose: that quarter's Rs 2.35bn share of Nations Trust Bank profit was 2.4 times June's and isn't explained, while the company's own profit fell 25%.

models.name: Dividend model
models.comment: Rs 6.50 / 7 / 7.50 next year, growing 5% / 8% / 10% (within the supported 11.4%) for five years; then EPS grows at 5% / 6% / 7% with the stable payout 1 − g ÷ ROE (55% / 52% / 50%), at the cost of equity.

models.name: Residual income
models.comment: Used instead of a cash-flow DCF: book Rs 395.47 plus returns above the 17.2% required return. ROE moves from 13% now to 11% / 12.5% / 14% over five years, 15% payout; with ROE below the cost of equity, each year subtracts value.

modelsNote: Four equity methods, all computed by scripts/valuation.py from modelInputs; no cash-flow DCF for a finance group. Growth check: 85.6% of profit kept × 13.3% ROE supports 11.4% growth; the 5% / 8% / 10% dividend growth and 5–7% long-run growth are below it in every case. Ratio check (docs/ratio-ranges.md): beta 0.87 and cost of equity 17.2% are in range; long-run growth is below the 12.24% bond yield; chosen P/Es are below the justified P/E. ROE of about 13% is below the 15% business-test level, explained by the surplus capital. Base EPS is 22% below the September quarter × 4, for the reason under P/E.

scenarios.common: Cost of equity from the house formula: risk-free 8.24% (12.24% bond less a 4.0% default spread) + beta 0.87 × (4.2% + 6.08% country premium). Starting NAV Rs 395.47 (30 Sep 2026); 227.35m shares. Base 2026/27 EPS of Rs 51 needs the second half about 8% above last year's Rs 20.59.

sensitivity.title: Residual income base case, Rs per share
sensitivity.note: Rs 215.25 is what a 17.2% cost of equity gives if long-run ROE settles at about 12.9%, close to today's 13%.

buyPlan.note: About Rs 90,787 in total, against Rs 107,625 for 500 shares at Rs 215.25. Today's price is just above fair value, so even the first tier waits for a small dip.
buyPlan.realism: Rs 178.43 is 17% below today's price and below every quarter's low since April 2025 (lowest Rs 207.75 in July–September 2026; Rs 208.00 in January–March 2026); the share was last there in April 2025 (Rs 167.00 low). Realistic only in a market-wide dip. Rs 157.43 needs a fall of about 27%.

fullText:
Summary: Central Finance (CFIN.N0000) is one of Sri Lanka's oldest vehicle-leasing and loan companies, and also owns 21.4% of Nations Trust Bank (19.72% of the votes) and half of Central Industries (PVC pipes). It is very safe: core capital 31.9% against a 10% minimum, equity about half of group assets, gross Stage 3 loans 1.79%, and group profit every year for at least ten years. Group EPS was Rs 45.09 in 2025/26 and Rs 28.73 in the six months to September 2026 (up 17%), but that rise came from the bank: the finance company's own profit fell 14% (25% in the September quarter) as interest costs rose 76% on new borrowing and impairment reversals dried up. At Rs 215.25 (CSE, 27 November 2026) the share is 0.54x group NAV of Rs 395.47 and 4.4x trailing EPS, which looks cheap, but with a group ROE of about 13% against the 17.2% a shareholder should demand (beta 0.87), a discount to book is deserved. Four equity methods put fair value at Rs 209.91 (was Rs 219.30), so the price is about 2.5% above it: fair. I'd buy at up to Rs 178.43 and treat Rs 157.43 or lower as a strong buy. It passes three of the four business tests (fails only on returns), so it stays on the watch list.

Price and key figures
Price: Rs 215.25, CSE close on 27 November 2026. July–September 2026 range Rs 207.75–240.00; 2025/26 range Rs 167.00–319.75.
Six months to September 2026 (group, unaudited): profit to shareholders Rs 6.53bn, up 17%; EPS Rs 28.73 against Rs 24.50. Share of Nations Trust Bank profit Rs 3.33bn (up 44%; Rs 2.35bn in the September quarter). Finance company alone: profit Rs 2.86bn, down 14%; interest expenses up 76%; impairment reversal Rs 0.26bn against Rs 0.90bn.
2025/26 (group, audited): profit to shareholders Rs 10.25bn, EPS Rs 45.09, NAV Rs 375.23. Company profit Rs 6.04bn, ROE 10.52%, gross NPL 1.65%, core capital 35.95%. Dividend Rs 6.50 (Rs 2.75 interim + Rs 3.75 final).
Balance sheet at September 2026 (group): leases, hire purchase and loans Rs 118.9bn (Rs 104.8bn in March), deposits Rs 51.2bn, borrowings Rs 29.9bn, owners' equity Rs 89.9bn, NAV Rs 395.47. Company core capital 31.86%, gross Stage 3 1.79%, Stage 3 coverage 59%.

Required return: 8.24% risk-free + beta 0.87 × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 17.2% (bear 18.7%, bull 15.7%). The beta weights the finance business (0.97), the Nations Trust Bank share (0.70) and Central Industries (0.90) by their H1 profit.

Valuation table (Rs per share)
Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted
Justified price to book | 173.2 | 229.5 | 318.2 | 230.3
P/E on 2026/27 earnings | 161.0 | 229.5 | 308.0 | 224.7
Dividend model | 120.9 | 179.9 | 272.6 | 180.8
Residual income | 144.3 | 202.2 | 297.5 | 203.9
Average | 149.9 | 210.3 | 299.1 | 209.9

Assumptions (bear / base / bull)
Cost of equity 18.7% / 17.2% / 15.7%; long-run ROE 11% / 12.5% / 14%; growth 5% / 6% / 7%; 2026/27 EPS 46 × 3.5 / 51 × 4.5 / 56 × 5.5; next dividend Rs 6.50 / 7 / 7.50 growing 5% / 8% / 10% for five years, then the stable payout 1 − g ÷ ROE. Base EPS is above the Rs 49.32 twelve-month figure but 22% below the September quarter × 4, because that quarter's Rs 2.35bn bank contribution (2.4 times June's) isn't explained and the company's own profit fell 25%.
Growth check: 85.6% of profit kept × 13.3% ROE supports 11.4% growth; every scenario is below it.

Business tests: 3 of 4 passed (capital, steady profit, dividends; fails returns at about 13%), so it's a good business at about a fair price: watch list (category 2, unchanged).

Management: the 2025/26 report promised disciplined loan growth, longer-term funding and no slip in asset quality. Loans grew 13% in H1 and funding shifted to borrowings as planned, but costs rose faster than income (company costs up 22%, income up 9%), and Stage 3 coverage fell to 59%.

Shareholders: Corporate Services (Pvt) Ltd A/C 1 16.11%, E.H. Wijenaike 15.41%, EPF 10.00%; public holding 63.60% with 6,847 public holders. Little change in July–September.

500-share plan
150 shares up to Rs 209.91, 200 up to Rs 178.43, 150 up to Rs 157.43: about Rs 90,787 in total. Rs 178.43 is 17% below today's price and below every quarter's low since April 2025 (lowest Rs 207.75 in July–September 2026; Rs 208.00 in January–March 2026); the share was last there in April 2025 (Rs 167.00 low). Realistic only in a market-wide dip. Rs 157.43 needs a fall of about 27%.
